title: V8 GC versus CLR garbage collection
hook: Both V8 and the CLR use tracing generational garbage collectors, but V8 runs inside a single-threaded agent with tight browser latency budgets while the CLR optimizes for server throughput and large object heaps.

blocks.text: **V8**: generational, Scavenge + mark-sweep-compact, incremental/concurrent marking, **orinoco** collector, no manual free. **CLR**: generational (gen 0/1/2), **LOH** for large objects, **POH** for pinned objects, background GC server/workstation modes, **finalizers** and **IDisposable** idioms. Both trace from roots — not refcount primary.

entries.plainDefinition: Mark reachable from roots; sweep rest.
CLR heap for objects >= 85KB — collected less often.
Split marking work across time slices.

blocks.text: C# developers moving to Node expect IDisposable everywhere — JS uses try/finally and explicit destroy() for scarce resources (sockets, file handles). CLR server GC uses multiple threads; V8 GC pauses block the one event loop thread.

blocks.title: Resource vs memory
blocks.body: GC frees unreachable objects — closing a file socket is still manual in both ecosystems.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Expecting deterministic destructors in JS. Forcing GC in production. Ignoring LOH fragmentation in C# when comparing only V8.

blocks.text: Interview cross-language: Promise microtasks run during same thread as V8 GC pause — tail latency compound. CLR ValueType reduce heap pressure; JS has only primitives. Discuss WASM linear memory — separate from JS GC.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Says V8 uses refcounting. Thinks GC closes files. Cannot compare generations.

interviewTakeaways: Both tracing generational — not primary refcount.
V8 GC pause blocks single JS thread.
60s: Both mark-sweep family generational. V8 Scavenge + old gen. CLR gen0-2 + LOH. JS no destructor — close handles explicitly. Finalizers unreliable both sides.
Follow-up: why Node needs fh.close() if GC exists?
commonPitfalls: Weak: ignore event loop blocked by major GC.
Strong: tracing + generations + explicit resource close.
